stdout_tail:
**Finding: No — SMOTE does not change the >50K F1 score by more than 0.02.**

- **Primary split** (75/25 stratified, seed=42): F1 without resampling = 0.6816, with SMOTE = 0.6769 → difference = **-0.0047**
- **Stability check** (5×5 repeated stratified CV, 25 folds, seeds 100-104): mean difference = **-0.0004**, 95% CI **[-0.0022, 0.0014]**, worst single fold only ±0.009 — all comfortably inside the ±0.02 threshold.

Methodology: missing categorical values kept as an explicit "Missing" category (not dropped), ordinal encoding for categoricals (tree-model friendly), both models at library defaults, SMOTE applied only to the training fold. Full code is in `analysis.py`, results in `result.json`.

parsed_result.summary: Applying SMOTE to the training data does not meaningfully change the minority-class (>50K) F1 score for a default RandomForestClassifier: the difference was -0.0047 on a single held-out split and -0.0004 on average across 25 cross-validation folds, both far below the 0.02 threshold.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Mean F1 difference (SMOTE - no resampling), 5x5 repeated stratified CV
parsed_result.direction: No practically significant difference; SMOTE roughly equivalent to no resampling for this model/metric
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Missing values in workclass/occupation/native-country (encoded as NaN, originally '?') were kept as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped, to preserve sample size. Categorical features were ordinal-encoded (not one-hot), a common and defensible choice for tree-based models. Class '>50K' (23.9% of data) treated as the positive/minority class. Primary evaluation used a single stratified 75/25 train/test split (seed=42) with RandomForestClassifier() and SMOTE() both at default hyperparameters, SMOTE applied only to the training fold. F1 computed on the positive (>50K) class only.
parsed_result.verification_method: 5x repeated 5-fold stratified cross-validation (25 total train/test folds) using 5 different random seeds (100-104), computing the paired F1 difference (SMOTE - no resampling) per fold, plus a 95% CI on the mean difference via normal approximation.
parsed_result.verification_result: Finding held up. Across 25 folds, no-resampling F1 mean=0.6762 (sd=0.0060) vs SMOTE F1 mean=0.6759 (sd=0.0063); mean paired difference = -0.0004 with 95% CI [-0.0022, 0.0014], and even the largest single-fold difference (max=+0.0093, min=-0.0073) stayed well under the 0.02 threshold. Conclusion: SMOTE does not change minority-class F1 by more than 0.02 for this classifier/dataset.
